solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Anything Scottish showing style, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is carried round to the far end of the word, so the order rotates by one

parts.note: a touch is a characteristic manner or style, as in an artist's touch

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for any trace of Scottish flair in an outfit or a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the T at the front of TOUCH to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: OUCHT is a Scots dialect form of 'aught', meaning anything at all.

clue.text: Bort's mixed with another stone, nothing American (vulgarly loud?)

indicators.note: something mixed has been stirred together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: bort is low-grade diamond; the plural form is taken as letters
an opal is a gemstone
zero, shaped like the letter O
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A gem-dealer's recipe for blending two stones, with an odd bracketed aside about noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bracketed part: OBSTROPALOUS is a colloquial corruption of obstreperous, so 'vulgarly' marks the nonstandard form as well as the noisiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstreperous means noisy and unruly; this jocular mispronounced variant is labelled vulgar or illiterate in Chambers.

clue.text: Pound the beat, as copper with Lord Mayor regularly intervening …

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the second letter slots in after the next letter of the policeman
regularly means at regular intervals, so the first letter of the Lord Mayor goes in after the first letter of the policeman

parts.note: a cop is a police officer, as a copper is
L is the usual abbreviation for Lord, as in LM for Lord Mayor
M stands for Mayor in the abbreviation LM, Lord Mayor

explanation.surface: A police constable plodding the streets while the Lord Mayor keeps getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: LM, the abbreviation for Lord Mayor, is 'regularly intervening': L goes in after the C of COP, making CLOP, and M after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To clomp is to walk with a heavy, noisy tread, just what a constable pounding a beat does.

clue.text: … Appearing under hat, mostly straw

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed after, below the other piece
mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word hat itself, before it loses a letter
with the ellipsis, what appears is the Lord Mayor from the previous clue, abbreviated LM as before

explanation.surface: The Lord Mayor of the previous clue turns up wearing a hat made mostly of straw.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this clue to 2-down: its Lord Mayor (LM) is what appears 'under' HA, the hat cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: HALM is a variant spelling of haulm, the stalks or stems of crops used as straw.

clue.text: Show off whirling atlatl's like … i.e. unleashed (8, two words)

indicators.note: whirling sends the letters spinning into a new order

parts.note: an atlatl is a spear-thrower; the 's is read as 'has', joining it to what follows

indicators.note: i.e. unleashed means the letters i and e are let loose from the word like, leaving only its other two letters

parts.note: the word like, which keeps its L and K once its I and E are let go

explanation.surface: Someone showing off by whirling an Aztec spear-thrower around, the ellipsis trailing off into a loose i.e.
explanation.walkthrough: 'i.e. unleashed' lets the I and E go from LIKE, leaving LK; 'whirling' then mixes those two letters with the six of ATLATL.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk tall is to boast or speak grandiloquently, a verbal way of showing off.

clue.text: In which one takes a tour abroad round California?

definitions.text: In which one takes a tour abroad round California?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the state's abbreviation, holding it inside
abroad means astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters of a tour, to be rearranged
CA is the US postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A question about which vehicle a visitor uses to tour around California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges A TOUR to AUTOR, which goes 'round' CA. The whole clue also describes the vehicle, a motor car for a touring trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocar is an old word for a motor car, the kind of vehicle you might take touring.

clue.text: Sedative that cuts a pain

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: mal is an old word for pain or sickness, as in mal de mer
an archaic written abbreviation of that, the Y standing for the old thorn letter

explanation.surface: A sedative that takes the edge off a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: YT for 'that' comes from old manuscripts, like ye for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amytal is a trade name for amobarbital, a barbiturate drug used as a sedative.

clue.text: Big dog that's tucked into potato salad

indicators.note: tucked into means sitting inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the end of potato and start of salad

explanation.surface: A large hound tucking into the picnic potato salad.
explanation.definitionFit: The tosa is a large Japanese breed of mastiff-type dog, originally bred for fighting.

clue.text: Church primate to the French, in his mitre?

parts.note: standard abbreviation for church
an ape is a primate
French for 'to the' before a masculine noun

explanation.surface: An archbishop, the church's primate, speaking to the French while wearing his mitre.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate looks like an archbishop, but it is the animal sense; the question mark warns that a mitre is only one example of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is French for hat, and a mitre is a bishop's ceremonial hat.

clue.text: Veteran signing up state spoilt with cash, grand

definitions.note: veteran flags an old or obsolete sense of the word

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged out of its proper shape, so the letters of state are rearranged

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An old soldier enlisting in a state that showers recruits with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges STATE to ATTES. 'Veteran' is part of the definition, flagging an old sense rather than an old soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest was formerly to enrol a recruit for military service, so attesting meant enlisting.

clue.text: Don't sleep so much when brought before head, being uneasy

parts.note: to rest less is to sleep less
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Advice to someone anxious to cut back on sleep before facing the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is not the boss but a geographical head, a promontory or ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Restlessness is the state of being uneasy and unable to settle, a noun matching the gerund phrase.

clue.text: Bachelor careless about desk as container for articles not currently needed?

definitions.text: container for articles not currently needed?

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: about means going around something on both sides

parts.note: lax means slack or careless
an ambo is a pulpit or reading desk in early churches

explanation.surface: A slovenly single man keeps a box around his desk for stuff he doesn't need yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles means newspaper pieces, not just objects: a Balaam box is an editor's store of filler copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balaam box was a newspaper office's repository for unwanted or filler items kept until space needed filling.

clue.text: Cabin No. 3 gives this accommodation

indicators.note: accommodation means housing: the answer is lodged in the phrase, so the letters after it go too
the written-out phrase gives this answer, yielding it from within, so its front letters are shed

parts.note: the abbreviation written out in full as number three

explanation.surface: Cabin number three provides the sleeping accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer only appears once No. 3 is written out in full as NUMBER THREE: 'gives this accommodation' says the phrase houses it, so drop NUM (leaving BERTHREE) and REE.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a sleeping place or cabin on a ship or train.

clue.text: Tsotsi, artful, hugging stunner given latitude

indicators.note: hugging means holding something wrapped inside

parts.note: sly means cunning or artful
a knockout blow stuns
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A wily township thug embracing a beauty and given free rein.
explanation.walkthrough: Stunner suggests a beauty, but here it is the knockout punch; a tsotsi is a South African young street criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skolly is a South African word for a hooligan or petty gangster, the same as a tsotsi.

clue.text: Mugs for fresh brew

definitions.meaning: first meaning: studies hard, as in mugging up (... as a variant of swots)
second meaning: Scots word for new small beer or ale

explanation.walkthrough: Mugs look like drinking vessels for a brew, but here it is a verb, to cram for exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Swats is both a verb form for studying intensively and a Scots plural noun for newly brewed ale.

clue.text: E.g. pipeclay got from arable mixed with art (9, two words)

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pipeclay obtained by mixing farmland soil with artistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra alba is a name for white earthy minerals such as pipeclay, gypsum or kaolin.

clue.text: A PT term in training

indicators.note: being in training means being worked into shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of physical-training jargon met during gym training.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as both definition and wordplay: a trampet is indeed a gym term used in training.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampet is a small trampoline used in gymnastics for springing into vaults, equipment of physical training.

clue.text: Regarding golf shot, one going in, I have supposed

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: going in means being inserted into the word alongside

parts.note: a putt is a golf stroke on the green
a means one
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A golfer recounting a putt that went in, as they had supposed it would.
explanation.walkthrough: The A slips inside the golf shot between its two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputative is an old word for putative, meaning reputed or commonly supposed.

clue.text: Violet, possibly a Scot with meagre English

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish first name, one possible example
thin means scanty or meagre
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Violet might be a Scottish woman of slender English means.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet reads as a woman's name but is the colour; 'possibly' signals that Ian is just one example of a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ianthine is a rare adjective meaning violet-coloured, from the Greek for violet.

clue.text: Parisian suburb, unfortunately without river

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are taken away

parts.note: poorly means badly or unfortunately
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A Paris suburb that sadly has no river running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the Italian river from the front of the adverb to leave ORLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Orly is a commune south of Paris, best known for its airport.

clue.text: Predial broadcast, not to rely on hearsay?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: a word for relating to land or farms, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A farm report on the radio that one shouldn't trust as mere rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearsay normally means rumour; read literally it is what one hears said, and a lip-reader does without hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by watching the mouth instead of relying on the ears.

clue.text: Bone showing spite mum cracks

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: hate as malice or spite
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A spiteful mother breaking someone's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hamate is one of the carpal bones of the wrist, named for its hook.

clue.text: Private secretary pocketing currency unit in sets of three

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside

parts.note: standard abbreviation for private secretary
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: A dishonest private secretary pocketing cash in batches of three.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games a prial is three cards of the same rank, short for pair royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prial, from pair royal, is a set of three, especially three of a kind in cards.

clue.text: Old watch in lazar-house losing time

indicators.note: losing something means letting it drop out

parts.note: a spital is an old word for a hospital, especially one for lepers
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A clock in a leper hospital running slow.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch looks like a timepiece, which time seems to confirm, but it means a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Spial is an obsolete word for a spy or watcher, someone keeping watch.

clue.text: Master letting wowser in, making allowances

indicators.note: letting someone through the door admits them, pairing with the word after
in completes letting in: the admitted letters end up inside the other word

parts.note: baas is South African for master or boss
a wowser is an Australian killjoy, typically a teetotaller, TT

explanation.surface: A boss allowing a puritanical prude into the house and making concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Wowser is Australian slang for a puritanical killjoy, especially an anti-drink campaigner, hence TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Batta was an extra allowance paid to soldiers in India, so battas are allowances.

clue.text: Foreign birds creating match with coating switched

indicators.note: switched means the two outer letters trade places, so the T at the end now becomes S
the coating is the outer layer of the word, its end letters: the S at the front takes the place of the T

parts.note: to suit is to match, as colours suit each other

explanation.surface: Exotic birds whose plumage changes as part of a mating match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with coating switched' swaps the outer S and T of SUIT (via TUIT); the middle UI stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a New Zealand songbird, foreign from a British point of view.

clue.text: Means of examining altered plans involving courtyard

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the rearranged letters wrap round the courtyard
altered means changed, so the letters of plans are put in a new order

parts.note: a patio is a paved courtyard

explanation.surface: A doctor's methods of examination being redrawn around a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' and 'involving' both apply: the courtyard sits inside the reshuffled plans, splitting them three and two.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpations are examinations by touch, a medical method of checking organs with the hands.

clue.text: They get to work after rumination, when a way of working comes up

definitions.text: They get to work after rumination

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: as means when
taken as written
modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: Thinkers getting down to business after deep reflection, once a method emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumination looks like thinking, but it is chewing the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: The omasa are the third stomachs of ruminants, which process food after it has been chewed again.

clue.text: Have a terrific time, tiddly, lager without opener freely consumed (7, two words)

indicators.note: drunk freely, the letters are loosened into a new order
without its opener means missing the first letter

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
the beer, before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A tipsy partygoer having a great time downing lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Large it is British slang for partying hard and enjoying oneself.

clue.text: When to hear vespers and an extract from Genesis

indicators.note: an extract is a piece lifted out of a longer text

parts.note: the middle letters of the book's name

explanation.surface: Evening services with a reading from Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a variant of e'ens, poetic for evenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening office, so evenings are when one would hear it.

clue.text: Orderly schoolkids cut pot

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the word loses its end

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot

explanation.surface: Well-behaved pupils trimming a cooking pot in class.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, croc for short.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc, short for crocodile, is a double file of children walking along in orderly fashion.

clue.text: Ester of a kind found in whole ingredients

indicators.note: found in means located inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the two words

explanation.surface: A chemist spotting a particular ester among wholefood ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Olein is a glyceride of oleic acid, an ester found in many natural fats and oils.

clue.text: Screed maybe I loaded into truck

indicators.note: loaded into means put inside as cargo

parts.note: truck is an old word for barter or trade, as in having no truck with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long written rant, perhaps one I loaded onto a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Truck looks like a vehicle, the load picture, but it is the dealing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long harangue, and a tirade is a long angry speech of that kind.

clue.text: Discoloration from some anils, processed

indicators.note: processed means put through treatment that changes the form

parts.note: anils are indigo plants

explanation.surface: Staining caused by processing indigo plants for dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanosis is abnormal dark pigmentation of body tissue, a medical kind of discoloration.

clue.text: We enjoy hurting street in grip of sober lives

parts.note: sad in the sense of serious or sober

indicators.note: in the grip of means held tightly inside

parts.note: is means exists or lives
standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A confession from people who like inflicting pain, about street life seized by grim sobriety.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase the answer could say of itself: sadists are those who enjoy hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadists take pleasure in inflicting pain, so 'we enjoy hurting' is their own self-description.

clue.text: Distinct botanical items died in broken case

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
broken means smashed apart, so the letters of case are rearranged

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A specimen case broken open, the plants in it dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns CASE into ECAS, with D going 'in' before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecad is a plant form adapted to its habitat, a distinct ecological type in botany.
